newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Norway to pick up bill for U.N. Cyprus talks.
newsitem.headline: Norway to pick up bill for U.N. Cyprus talks.

text.p: Norway will pick up the bill for U.N.-sponsored talks between the leaders of the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities scheduled for July 9 to 13 at a rural resort about 90 miles (145 kms) north of New York City, a member of the Norwegian U.N. mission confirmed on Thursday.
The cost was expected to be between $30,000 and $40,000.

He said Norway had been approached by the financially hard-pressed U.N. secretariat to cover the expenses of the encounter between Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides, who heads the Greek Cypriot community, and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash at a resort and conference centre called Troutbeck, near Amenia, New York.

The two leaders are expected to be accompanied by only a couple of advisers each. Secretary-General Kofi Annan is scheduled to open the talks and then hand over to his special adviser for Cyprus, Diego Cordovez, a former Ecuadorean foreign minister.

The Norwegian official, whose country also provided facilities for ground-breaking talks at Oslo in 1993 between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation, said: "We are happy to contribute to an effort by the secretary-general to get talks going between the two parties on Cyprus."
